title: Possessing seven qualities, bhikkhus, Sāriputta controls his mind and does not let the mind control him. What seven? Here, bhikkhus, Sāriputta is skilled in concentration,…
content: Possessing seven qualities, bhikkhus, Sāriputta controls his mind and does not let the mind control him. What seven? Here, bhikkhus, Sāriputta is skilled in concentration, skilled in attaining concentration, skilled in abiding in concentration, skilled in emerging from concentration, skilled in the comfort of concentration, skilled in the range of concentration, and skilled in inducing concentration. Possessing these seven qualities, bhikkhus, Sāriputta controls his mind and does not let the mind control him.

title: Having approached, that devata spoke these verses to the Venerable Nāgadatta: Nāgadatta, Enter the village at the proper time, And when you return from the…
content:
Having approached, that devata spoke these verses to the Venerable Nāgadatta:

Nāgadatta,
Enter the village at the proper time,
And when you return from the village,
Return early.
You live too involved
With laypeople,
Overcome by too many
Feelings of pain and pleasure.
I fear that Nāgadatta,
This reckless one,
Will be bound and fettered
By household affairs.
Do not fall into
The power of Death,
How can one escape
Māra's control?

The Venerable Nāgadatta, stirred by that devata, was greatly moved.

title: - Bhikkhus, if wanderers of other sects should ask you: 'In what abiding, friends, does Samaṇa Gotama dwell much during the rains?' Being asked thus,…
content: - Bhikkhus, if wanderers of other sects should ask you: 'In what abiding, friends, does Samaṇa Gotama dwell much during the rains?' Being asked thus, bhikkhus, you should answer those wanderers: 'In the concentration of mindfulness of breathing, friends, the Blessed One dwells much during the rains.' Here, bhikkhus, mindful I breathe in, mindful I breathe out. Or breathing in long, I understand: 'I breathe in long'; or breathing out long, I understand: 'I breathe out long'; or breathing in short, I understand: 'I breathe in short'; or breathing out short, I understand: 'I breathe out short' ... 'Contemplating relinquishment, I breathe in,' I understand thus; 'Contemplating relinquishment, I breathe out,' I understand thus. Bhikkhus, one speaking rightly, if he were to say 'This is a noble abiding, this is a Brahmā abiding, this is the Tathāgata's abiding,' should say that the concentration of mindfulness of breathing is a noble abiding, a Brahmā abiding, the Tathāgata's abiding.

title: How, householder, is one who wanders without abode? The bondage of dwelling on the sign of form, householder, has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut…
content: How, householder, is one who wanders without abode? The bondage of dwelling on the sign of form, householder, has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made not to arise again, not to be born in the future. Therefore, the Tathāgata is called one who wanders without abode. The bondage of dwelling on the sign of sound... sign of odor... sign of taste... sign of touch... sign of mental object, householder, has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made not to arise again, not to be born in the future. Therefore, the Tathāgata is called one who wanders without abode. Thus, householder, is one who wanders without abode.

title: Elder Friend of Kuma's son: Wandering many places with the practice of non-thinking, Burning away jhāna — what is the use of wandering everywhere? Therefore,…
content:
Elder Friend of Kuma's son:

Wandering many places with the practice of non-thinking,
Burning away jhāna — what is the use of wandering everywhere?
Therefore, stop agitation; without agitation, meditate.

title: Elder Kuṭivihāri: Who is in the hut? A bhikkhu free from greed, His mind well concentrated. Know him, O good sir, The hut you built…
content:
Elder Kuṭivihāri:

Who is in the hut? A bhikkhu free from greed,
His mind well concentrated. Know him, O good sir,
The hut you built is not in vain.

title: Bhikkhus, for one who has developed and cultivated mindfulness of the body, whatever wholesome states are internal all belong to the component of true knowledge.…
content: Bhikkhus, for one who has developed and cultivated mindfulness of the body, whatever wholesome states are internal all belong to the component of true knowledge. Just as, bhikkhus, the great ocean, if one pervades it with the mind, all rivers that flow into it belong to the great ocean. So too, bhikkhus, for one who has developed and cultivated mindfulness of the body, whatever wholesome states are internal all belong to the component of true knowledge.

title: ( Yakkha ): How to cross the flood? How to cross the great ocean? How to escape suffering? How to be purified? ( Blessed One…
content:
( Yakkha ):
How to cross the flood?
How to cross the great ocean?
How to escape suffering?
How to be purified?

( Blessed One ):
With faith, cross the flood.
With heedfulness, cross the ocean.
With energy, escape suffering.
With wisdom, be purified.

title: From whom a person learns the Dhamma, Let him pay homage to that person as the devas pay homage to Inda. That one, being honored,…
content:
From whom a person learns the Dhamma,
Let him pay homage to that person as the devas pay homage to Inda.
That one, being honored, with joyful mind,
Having learned much, proclaims the true Dhamma.

An attentive, wise person, reflecting,
Practicing Dhamma in accordance with Dhamma,
Becomes learned, intelligent, and careful.
By serving such a one, he becomes not heedless.

title: Bhikkhus, these four kinds of persons exist and are found in the world. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a person has attained internal serenity of mind…
content: Bhikkhus, these four kinds of persons exist and are found in the world. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a person has attained internal serenity of mind but not the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena. Here, bhikkhus, a person has attained the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena but not internal serenity of mind. Here, bhikkhus, a person has attained neither internal serenity of mind nor the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena. Here, bhikkhus, a person has attained both internal serenity of mind and the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena. Bhikkhus, these four kinds of persons exist and are found in the world.
